lessons.title: The module and the session
lessons.why: The shell is how you read effective policy and how you assign compliance recording. The portal will not show you every object.
body: Install the MicrosoftTeams module and connect it to the tenant you named in the foundations track. Confirm you are not in production. Cmdlet parameters move between module versions, so Get-Help in the version you are about to run beats a blog post.
Compliance recording policies are created and granted in this module. If you only learn the portal, you cannot finish a recorder design.
lessons.say: I connect the MicrosoftTeams module to a named tenant and read help before I change anything.
lessons.fault: A script from last year removes numbers because a parameter changed meaning.
lessons.listen: Use the MicrosoftTeams module in a lab tenant. Read Get-Help for the version you are running.

lessons.title: Objects you will actually get
lessons.why: Voice routing is a handful of objects. If you can draw them, the cmdlets are spelling.
body: A dial plan holds normalization rules. A voice route holds a pattern and gateways. A PSTN usage is a name that ties routes to a policy. A voice routing policy is the ordered list of usages you grant to a user. A PSTN gateway is the paired SBC.

Application instances show up twice in real designs: resource accounts for voice apps, and bots for compliance recording. Confirm which object you are creating before you run New-CsOnlineApplicationInstance.

chart.title: Object count in a small design
chart.note: How many objects, not how many users.

lessons.say: Usage, route, policy, gateway. The policy is what the user has. The route is what the pattern does.
lessons.fault: A route exists and no policy grants a usage that contains it.
lessons.listen: Remember gateway, route, usage, and policy. The user only sees the policy you granted.

lessons.title: Grant, set, and new
lessons.why: New creates, set changes, grant assigns. Mixing them up is how a policy is edited and never reaches the user.
body: New-CsOnlineVoiceRoute creates a route. Set-CsOnlinePstnUsage maintains the usage list. Grant-CsOnlineVoiceRoutingPolicy assigns a policy to a user. Grant-CsTeamsComplianceRecordingPolicy assigns a recorder policy. None of those verbs is a synonym.
Read with Get- before you Set- or Grant-. Then read again. The second read is the evidence pack, not a personality trait.

chart.title: Verbs
chart.note: Do not skip the last read.

lessons.say: Grant assigns to a user. Set changes an object. I read both times.
lessons.fault: The policy text is correct and the user still has Global.
lessons.listen: New creates, set changes, grant assigns. Read the user after you grant.

lessons.title: Reading a user before you change one
lessons.why: The pilot user is often not the user you think. Group assignment hides the policy you just edited.
body: Get-CsOnlineUser shows voice policy, dial plan, and number fields. Look at the effective values. A group grant can beat the direct assignment you remember from last quarter.
Test the call as that user, from the client they actually use. A browser join and a certified phone do not take the same media path, and QoS will not treat them the same either.

lessons.title: When the portal and the shell disagree
lessons.why: The toast is not the directory. The directory is what the next call will use.
body: If the Teams admin center shows a policy and the shell shows another, believe the shell long enough to place a test call, then refresh both. Replication delay is real. An hour of firmware changes during that delay is not.
Write down the time, the cmdlet, and the values. That note is the evidence pack. It is also how you avoid changing three systems because one screen was stale.
lessons.say: I will trust a fresh Get- over a stale toast, then place one test call.
lessons.fault: Three changes land during a replication delay and nobody knows which one worked.
lessons.listen: If the portal and the shell disagree, read the shell, wait, and place one test call.

lessons.title: Safety on a lab tenant
lessons.why: Certificate and routing experiments belong where a mistake cannot take the company’s numbers away.
depends: A second tenant or a clearly named lab domain
body: Pair a lab SBC to a lab domain. Use obviously fake names. Contoso and 555 numbers exist so practice does not point at a real directory. Do not find-and-replace a lab script onto production without reading every name.
Production changes get one hypothesis, a rollback, and a window. The lab is where you learn that a private CA will not satisfy Direct Routing.
lessons.say: I will not discover certificate behavior on the company trunk.
lessons.fault: The lab FQDN is also the production FQDN.
lessons.listen: Experiment in a lab tenant. Do not point a practice script at production by find-and-replace.
